title: Staged Terraform pipelines with incremental policy evaluation and drift-aware linting for Private deployments
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Summary:
Add a gated, staged Terraform CI pipeline tailored for Private (VPC) deployments that runs fast linting, incremental policy-as-code checks (Conftest/OPA), and a drift-aware pre-apply gating stage. The pipeline should scale checks by changed module, reduce developer wait time, and produce actionable diagnostics for remediation.

Goals:
- Run formatting and static linting (tflint/terraform fmt) on the modified directories within a PR within 2 minutes.
- Execute policy-as-code in two passes: quick local-rule validation (Conftest) on changed files, then full OPA/rego evaluation against a synthetized plan artifact for high-risk resources.
- Introduce a drift-aware pre-apply health check that queries deployed state and warns/fails if existing infra drift exceeds thresholds (e.g., security group wide-opening, public subnet changes).
- Gate apply with explicit approval for high-risk changes detected by OPA rules and provide auto-rollforward options for low-risk fixes.
- Integrate results into GitHub checks, Redwood Console dashboard, and Slack channel #infra-ci.

Non-goals:
- Replacing runtime runtime-level canary deployments for application code.
- Full refactor of existing Terraform modules (we'll add opt-in hooks instead).

Acceptance criteria:
- Pull requests touching terraform/ or modules/ only run the minimal lint/checks for the changed paths and full policy evaluation for plan files.
- Policy failures produce a Conftest/OPA formatted report linking to exact resource blocks and recommended remediations.
- Drift check returns a pass/warn/fail with clear thresholds and is configurable per-environment.
- CI config committed and tested in ci/terraform-pipelines.yml with a GitHub check that blocks merge on P1 policy failures.
- Documentation page in Confluence and a short runbook for on-call.

Implementation approach:
1) Modify repo CI to detect changed Terraform paths in a PR using git diff. Use a fast preflight job that runs terraform fmt -check and tflint only against those directories.
2) Generate a synthetic plan artifact in a sandbox workspace (terraform plan -out=plan.binary) and export JSON (terraform show -json) for the policy engine.
3) Run Conftest on changed files for immediate feedback (Rego + local assertions). For the plan JSON, run a full OPA rego bundle evaluation. We will reuse existing rego bundles and add a small shim to map plan schema to our rules.
4) Implement a drift-aware job that queries the target state via terraform state pull / cloud provider API (read-only). Compare critical resource attributes against thresholds defined in a per-environment config.
5) Add gating logic: low/medium issues are advisory with auto-labels and remediation suggestions; high-risk issues block merge and require approver group (infra-approvers).
6) Integrate with GitHub Checks API, Redwood Console (dashboard tile: "IaC Gate Failures"), and a Slack summary.

Trade-offs & risk notes:
- Running full OPA on every PR is expensive; incremental plan-based evaluation reduces cost but may miss cross-module interactions; mitigated by nightly full-eval.
- False positives from strict rules will slow teams; we will ship with a grace window and an "opt-out" tag for urgent fixes and monitor feedback.
- Drift-check read-only queries could add API pressure; use sampling and caching per-run.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: implement preflight lint and Conftest quick checks for a pilot repo (internal-vpc-templates).
- Week 2: add plan generation and plan-based OPA evaluation for the pilot.
- Week 3: enable drift-check and gating policies for pilot; collect metrics.
- Week 4: open opt-in for other infra repos, iterate on rules based on false-positive rate, and publish docs.

Monitoring & metrics:
- Measure PR execution time, policy failure rate, false-positive feedback (labelled), and mean-time-to-approve when blocked.
- Dashboard: CI failure rate, policy-block rate, drift-failures by environment.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRA/pages/Private+Terraform+CI+design
- RFC: https://docs.redwood.com/rfc/2026-03-staged-tf-ci
- Pipeline YAML (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-templates/blob/main/ci/terraform-pipelines.yml

Notes:
- We will coordinate with Security for the initial rego bundle to ensure high-risk checks are aligned with compliance controls.
- Include a periodic job to run full-rego-bundle against master to catch interactions missed by incremental checks.
